sonnet.problem: The question asks about gossips and slanderers (verses 29-30), but the only earlier card, card 11, tells just the first part of verse 29 ('wickedness, evil, greed and depravity'). Card 13 tells the gossips and slanderers only after this question. The choice card jumps ahead of what has been told, so the baker can't make an informed guess. The 'only… and says nothing' wording also gives away that the answer is False.
sonnet.rule: Cards follow the passage in order. A choice card can look back at a verse an earlier card in the same stop told, but never jumps ahead.

sonnet.problem: The right answer ('Futile thinking and darkened hearts') uses the Bible's own negative wording. The wrong answers ('Sharper thinking and stronger hearts', 'Quiet thinking and peaceful hearts') are plainly positive and don't sound like Scripture. The right answer stands out, and the question offers no real alternative to a negative outcome.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
